findings.text: assert receipt["run_id"] == run_id compares the receipt with the run id the test itself passed in, so both sides move together and the assertion holds whatever the product does; the guard against a regression is the phase assertion on line 266.

the head arm row names no head sha, writing "the run's head, as the manifest's after_suite.revision names it" instead, so the fragment alone cannot be told which revision passed and the base row beside it carries only an abbreviated sha.

the artifacts line says both arms ran as /usr/bin/sbatch --wait --partition=all_debug, but the run directory holds no scheduler receipt for the job that ran gate-arms.sh (the two *.log.scheduler sidecars are 0 bytes and belong to the shim attempts recorded in retry_failures), so the job property the done_when names is asserted rather than recorded.

notes: added_failure_count is 0 because the log the reviewed manifest's after_suite names carries '4 passed' and EXIT=0 with no FAILED id, while the baseline log carries the single failing id tests/test_complete_reports_every_refusal.py::test_the_dry_run_reports_three_refusals_and_an_invocation_that_promotes and EXIT=1. The derivation reads the log_path values in the reviewed manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite entries (base-test_complete_reports_every_refusal.log and head-test_complete_reports_every_refusal.log); crew's own captures baseline_suite-1795016885020370985.log and after_suite-1795016885873512485.log are 0 bytes because the sbatch shim failed, which the reviewed manifest records under retry_failures with a scaffolding attribution. Instrument positive control: the base log shows 4 collected tests and '1 failed, 3 passed', so the counter is shown seeing a non-zero population before the head arm's zero is reported.
